# tidystata

<!-- badges: start -->

[![Lifecycle: stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable) [![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/tidystata)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tidystata)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/socimh/tidystata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/socimh/tidystata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

<!-- badges: end -->

[tidystata](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/) brings Stata-style data exploration and preparation to R. Inspect variables, summarise measurements, tabulate categories and prepare new columns. Select variables with tidyselect helpers and calculate by group with `.by`. The resulting tables work with ordinary R tools for filtering, joining and plotting.

[中文介绍](https://github.com/socimh/tidystata/blob/master/README.zh.md)

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("socimh/tidystata")
```

## Core functions

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidystata)
library(dplyr)
```

### findit(): find the R equivalent of a Stata command

```{r}
findit(reg, robust)

findit("egen rowmean")
```

A bare command such as `findit(egen)` browses the whole family and shows up to
five operations. A specific query such as `findit("egen rowmean")` returns one
clear answer; ambiguous queries retain up to ten relevant candidates.
`print(n = Inf)` expands the returned results; use `findit(egen)` to browse
broader operations. Within a matching operation, recommendations prefer
tidystata, then tidyverse, then other packages or base R. Add variable names or
hints with commas, as in `findit(tab, sex, region)` or `findit(tab, gen)`.
You can also supply Stata text: ``findit(`tab sex region`, row)`` and
`findit("tab sex region, row")` customize the same row-percentage example.
To look up one command from a do-file, highlight it and run the **Find Stata
equivalent** addin (`findit_selection()`), or copy it and run `findit_clip()`.
These helpers print results in the console and require the optional rstudioapi
and clipr packages, respectively.
Every entry is listed by topic in [Coming from Stata](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/coming-from-stata.html).

### codebook(): describe every variable

```{r}
codebook(lifeexp)
```

### summ(): summary statistics

`lexp:safewater` selects the three consecutive variables from `lexp` through `safewater`, including both endpoints. Other tidyselect helpers such as `ends_with()` and `matches()`, or a Stata-style `varlist()`, also work.

```{r}
summ(lifeexp, lexp:safewater, .by = region)
```

### tab(), tab1() and tab2(): frequency tables

Use region and a second category derived from `lifeexp`: whether life expectancy is at least 70 years. `region:lexp_70` selects these two columns.

`tab()` counts each observed combination, with percentages.

```{r}
lifeexp_tab <- lifeexp |>
  transmute(region, lexp_70 = lexp >= 70)

tab(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70)
```

`tab1()` returns a named list with a separate frequency table for each variable.

```{r}
tab1(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70)
```

`tab2()` displays the joint counts as a cross-table, with region in rows and life expectancy category in columns.

```{r}
tab2(lifeexp_tab, region:lexp_70)
```

You can also tabulate continuous variables. When there are many distinct values, use `print_headtail()` to see the beginning and end or `print_interval()` to inspect evenly spaced rows. These helpers shorten the display while retaining the complete table.

```{r}
tab(lifeexp, lexp) |> print_headtail()

tab(lifeexp, lexp) |> print_interval()
```

## Learn more

tidystata also includes `stata_recode()`, `destring()`, `encode()`, `decode()`, `tostring()`, the `row_*()` and `duplicates_*()` families, `stata_lag()`, `stata_lead()`, `stata_diff()`, `corr()`, `pwcorr()`, `misstable()`, `isid()`, `stata_merge()`, `xtile()` and `preview()`. See the guides below for examples and output conventions.

- [Getting started](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/getting-started.html): a short workflow.
- [Inspect and prepare data](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/inspect-and-prepare.html): clean measurements, check keys and combine records.
- [Tabulate and compare categories](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/tabulation.html): the `tab()` and `fre()` families.
- [Summarise measurements](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/summary-statistics.html): `summ()`, `tabstat()` and correlations.
- [Containers and missing values](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/containers-and-missing-values.html): return types, grouping and labels.
- [Reference](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/index.html): every function.
